Gnosis Interpretation
MOVE measures Treasury volatility and term-premium stress: below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress; 105.20 is moderate. SOFR is secured overnight funding (3.89% effective Oct 5), not a stand-alone stress verdict. NFCI at -0.548 indicates looser broad financial conditions. The 10Y Treasury yield closed at 5.27% on Oct 6, down 4 bp from Oct 5.

Fed & Policy Watch
FOMC minutes are due today at 2:00 PM ET; read for the Committee's balance of risks and rate-path discussion, not as a policy decision. The next top-tier inflation catalyst in this horizon is September CPI on Oct 14 at 8:30 AM ET. The Fed Board calendar sets the Oct 14 Beige Book at 2:00 PM ET; a Chicago Fed calendar listing showed 3:00 PM, so the Board's central release calendar is used for the system publication time.
Omissions and Watch
  • BLS direct monthly schedule returned HTTP 403. Its current CPI release page independently confirms Sep CPI for Oct 14 at 8:30 AM ET. PPI is scheduled Oct 15, outside this briefing window; no other BLS event inferred.
  • No BEA release verified through Oct 14. EIA weekly Petroleum Status Report is shifted to Oct 15 at noon ET for the Columbus Day week, outside the window; no Wednesday petroleum inventory release is inferred.
  • Oct 12 is a Federal Reserve and fixed-income holiday; NYSE is open and CME publishes a holiday schedule. Treasury bills due Oct 13 are date-only on the tentative schedule; exact notices/times were not available at cutoff.
  • Geopolitical/policy risks remain unscheduled watch items; no timed event is invented.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
ES is modestly higher overnight; the 10Y yield eased 4 bp and MOVE remains in the moderate band. FOMC minutes, the 10Y auction, and energy updates can drive intraday repricing. Let ES and rates confirm before acting; scenario framework, not a directional call.
INVALIDATION
Reassess if ES breaks and holds beyond its overnight range with confirming yield/volatility repricing, or if auction demand/minutes materially shift the rates outlook. CPI on Oct 14 is the next major scheduled inflation catalyst; this is not a trade signal.
